title: I shipped my first game with AI, released ~20 updates in six weeks, and still don’t know how to find players
author: zamzor
selftext:
I’ve been a software engineer for 10 years, with the last six working in Unity and game development, mostly VR, AR and 3D. I started an agency, and until recently all our work was for B2B clients.



Dead Mile was the first game I produced for our own players. I started it as a vibe-coding project. I knew how to build software, but I had very little experience getting a game in front of people.



For the development side: Unity AI helped with much of the code. I used AI for backgrounds, UI portraits, music and voices, alongside licensed character sprite packs. That let me move quickly, but shipping the first version was only the start. I’ve released around 20 versions in the past month and a half.



The useful part of the process has been watching what players actually do. I’m using PostHog to understand player behaviour and feed that back into changes to the gameplay loop. I now have some players still coming back three weeks after they started. That’s encouraging, although I’m still working out how to turn it into a sustainable game.



Distribution is where I’m stuck. Dead Mile got much more attention on unofficial/modded markets, while the official Google Play and App Store releases are getting roughly 20–30 organic installs a day. I tried Meta ads: around $300 spent, with about $60 in in-app purchases coming into the game. I can’t keep relying on that approach.



I’ve also built several other mobile games over the past month and had encouraging feedback from players. Getting them in front of the right people is the part I haven’t figured out.



For people here who’ve taken an AI-assisted game beyond the development stage: what brought you your first steady stream of real players? What would you test first with a tiny audience—small creators, a different way of showing the game, store-page changes, or something else?



And how did you decide whether you had a discovery problem or still needed to improve the game itself? I’d really appreciate hearing what worked for you, including things you tried that went nowhere.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
if you are getting 20-30 installs a day, that is not really a distribution issue imo. 

what are the players saying? Google Play console also have a lot of metrics tracked for you.

I feel like it may be a real distribution issue if you are getting high rating but the traffic is small.

replies.author: zamzor
replies.body:
Fair point. The store feedback has been positive: Google Play’s US listing shows 4.8/5 with 43 reviews, and the App Store is at 4.5/5 from 15 ratings across all countries. One Android player described it as ‘calm yet fun’, which was useful feedback about what they actually enjoy.



I’m still separating that from retention and monetisation—good ratings alone don’t answer those. I’m using PostHog alongside the store metrics to understand where people drop out and who comes back.



The question I’m trying to answer is how to reach more of the players who enjoy that slower, tactical loop. Which store or retention metric would you look at first to decide whether discovery is the next thing to work on?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I think you went further than I am as a dev atm, so I dont have answers for you.

maybe it is a monetization issue because it sounds like the ads are bring in players but they aren't spending enough (or they aren't playing long enough to spend more)

comments.author: Disastrous-Gain5870
comments.body: 20-30 installs a day and you have a distribution issue? Huh?

replies.author: zamzor
replies.body: Yes—by low value I mean the revenue coming from that volume of installs. I’m seeing roughly $2–$3 a day in in-app purchases and around $0.30 in ads. To me, that’s encouraging evidence that some players enjoy it enough to spend money in it. The question I’m trying to answer is how to multiply that traction a thousandfold. Where would you start?

replies.author: eduo
replies.body:
Problem is that a whole swathe of games can't support living through IAPs or Ads. I don't have good advice on how to do this but it should be possible to understand if your app/game has reached its stable audience and won't attract more.

Do you have close friends who can play it and give honest feedback? More often than not we have testflights where it's already visible in the testflight numbers that the game is not piquing users' interest (they won't say anything, as most testflight beta testers are drive-by-users).

comments.author: mentiondesk
comments.body: I’d focus on connecting directly with niche communities that care about your genre. Join discussions on Reddit or gaming Discords to get honest feedback and tap into micro audiences. Finding conversations where potential players hang out can make a difference. One tool I tried for this is ParseStream, which alerts you instantly when people discuss topics or keywords relevant to your game so you can jump in at the right time.

replies.author: zamzor
replies.body: I’ve actually been posting about the game around Reddit and Discord servers, using tracked URLs, but those links haven’t shown me any attributed installs from those channels so far. That’s the part I’m struggling with. Have you found a particular kind of post or community interaction that gets people from a discussion into actually trying the game?

replies.author: Early_Flamingo5337
replies.body: not at all, in this communities there are more people advertising their games than people interested on playing them

comments.author: getplaytests-dot-dev
comments.body: You could try using us to get some feedback and see if there's something you could improve with the game to keep your players playing

comments.author: Ok_Inspector100
comments.body: Maybe you just made a shit game?

replies.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
replies.body: If he’s getting installs then people want tot play the game. He’s just not good at marketing.

comments.author: WickedDelight
comments.body: You should send dm to YouTubers, twitch streamers that specialize in gameplay content that play games like your games, that also have decent amount of followers. Invite them to play your game etc. They sometimes do random indie gameplay and may feature you a little in one of their sessions. A viral moment online during their play maybe a catapult moment for your game. Just a thought.
